payload.task_text:
You are a tech lead at a software company. Your manager has asked you to compile a technology trend report based on the most popular recent videos from a well-known programming education channel called Fireship on the video platform. You need to analyze the top 10 most-viewed videos from 2024 to 2025, summarize technology trends, publish findings to the team knowledge base, schedule a recurring review meeting, and notify the team by email.

Your workflow should proceed as follows.

First, search the video platform for the Fireship channel and retrieve its videos. Sort the videos by popularity and select the top 10 by view count. For each of those videos, collect the following details: the video identifier, the title, the publication date, the duration in seconds, the view count, the like count, and the primary technology topic derived from the video tags or title keywords.

Second, create a spreadsheet file named Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx. Inside this file, create a sheet named Videos containing one row per video with the following columns in order: Video_ID, Title, Published_Date, Duration_Seconds, View_Count, Like_Count, Primary_Topic. Then create a second sheet named Topic_Summary. In Topic_Summary, aggregate the data by topic and include these columns: Topic, Video_Count, Total_Views, Avg_Duration. Each row should represent one distinct technology topic found across the top 10 videos. Ensure the averages and totals are correctly computed.

Third, create a new page in the team knowledge base titled "Fireship Tech Trends Q1 2026". Add a brief introductory heading and a paragraph summarizing the overall findings. Then add a table or structured block listing the top 5 technology topics by total view count, with their video counts and total views.

Fourth, check the shared calendar for any existing Tech Review events in March 2026. Then create a new weekly recurring meeting event titled "Tech Review Meeting" scheduled for Monday March 9 2026 from 14:00 to 15:00. Use the UTC timezone.

Fifth, send an email to techteam@company.com. The subject should reference the tech trend report. The body should summarize which technology topics appeared most in the top videos, mention the new meeting scheduled, and inform the team that the full report is available in Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx.

The channel configuration file in your workspace is named channel_config.json and contains guidance on which channel to use, the date range of interest, how many videos to include, and the report title. An email template is also provided in email_template.txt to help you format the outgoing message.

When all outputs are complete, claim the task as done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep the Fireship catalog on explore, then parallelize the independent workbook, Notion, and calendar artifacts. The email stays with the main agent. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins.

Before Wave 1, the main agent reads `channel_config.json` and `email_template.txt` in read-only mode and freezes the channel, 2024-2025 date range, top-10 count, and report title.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 explore sub-agent:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Locate the Fireship channel and retrieve its full video list; filter to videos published between 2024-01-01 and 2025-12-31 inclusive, sort by view count descending, and select the top 10 (or all available if fewer than 10). For each selected video collect `video_id`, `title`, `published_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `duration_seconds`, `view_count`, `like_count`, and a concise `primary_topic` technology label derived from the video tags or, if tags are unavailable, the title keywords. Return the compact ten-row table plus channel/page/date/count controls. Do not write files or create deliverables.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies the date window and ranking, aggregates Topic_Summary (`Topic, Video_Count, Total_Views, Avg_Duration`), and freezes one canonical packet of the top-10 video rows and topic totals. Missing catalog coverage is a blocker.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of `Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx`. Read only the frozen packet. Create a `Videos` sheet holding exactly 10 data rows (one per video, in the given order) with columns `Video_ID, Title, Published_Date, Duration_Seconds, View_Count, Like_Count, Primary_Topic` in that order, and a `Topic_Summary` sheet with one row per distinct `Primary_Topic` giving `Video_Count`, `Total_Views`, and `Avg_Duration` (rounded to at most 2 decimals) computed from the frozen Videos data. If the video data is incomplete, build the workbook with the valid rows. Write literal values and read every populated range back.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole Notion owner of a page titled exactly `Fireship Tech Trends Q1 2026`. Search the exact title first, create at most once on zero matches, and block on duplicates. Include an `Overview` heading with a summary paragraph covering the 10 videos analyzed in 2024-2025, the most frequent topic(s) by video count, and the top topic by total views. Add a `Top 5 Technology Topics by Total Views` section with a table of Topic, Video_Count, and Total_Views for the top 5 topics sorted by Total_Views descending. Read the page back.
   3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Sole calendar owner. Search existing `Tech Review` events in March 2026, then create a weekly recurring event titled `Tech Review Meeting` starting Monday 2026-03-09 from 14:00 to 15:00 UTC, repeating every Monday at that time. If an identical event (same title, start time, and weekly recurrence) already exists, treat it as the deliverable instead of creating a duplicate. Read the retained event back.

After Wave 2, the main agent reconciles the workbook, Notion page, and calendar event against the same packet. In that same response, search Sent mail for exact To `techteam@company.com` with a subject that references the tech trend report, send at most once using `email_template.txt` and the frozen findings (most frequent topics, the new meeting, and that the full report is in `Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx`), then read it back. Do not dispatch more sub-agents.

nodes.text:
You are researching YouTube data for a tech trend report. Use ONLY the YouTube MCP tools available to you (mcp__youtube__channels_listVideos, mcp__youtube__channels_navigateList, mcp__youtube__videos_getVideo, mcp__youtube__videos_searchVideos).

GOAL: Find the top 10 most-viewed videos published in calendar years 2024–2025 (publishedAt between 2024-01-01 and 2025-12-31) from the YouTube channel "Fireship" (channelId: UCsBjURrPoezykLs9EqgamOA).

STEPS:
1. Call mcp__youtube__channels_listVideos with channelId "UCsBjURrPoezykLs9EqgamOA", sortOrder "popular", maxResults 20. This starts a list session sorted by popularity (view count).
2. If the list session contains fewer than ~20 videos, or if many of the first 20 are outside 2024-2025, use mcp__youtube__channels_navigateList to browse additional pages (the listId is returned from the listVideos call) so you can identify the most-viewed videos within the 2024–2025 window. Try to cover at least 40-60 of the most popular videos to be safe.
3. For every candidate video whose publishedAt falls within 2024-01-01 .. 2025-12-31, call mcp__youtube__videos_getVideo with the videoId and parts ["snippet", "contentDetails", "statistics"] to obtain: title, publishedAt, duration (ISO 8601 format e.g. PT1H2M3S — convert to total seconds), viewCount, likeCount, and tags (may be empty).
4. Select the TOP 10 videos by viewCount among those published in 2024–2025.
5. For each of the top 10, determine a PRIMARY_TOPIC (a short technology topic, e.g. "AI", "Web Development", "DevOps", "Programming Languages", "Cloud", "Security", "Databases", etc.) derived from the video's tags and/or title keywords. Choose the single most relevant topic per video. Do not invent topics — base them on the tags/title.

DELIVERABLE — return a structured report containing, for each of the 10 videos, one line/entry with EXACTLY these fields:
- video_id
- title
- published_date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- duration_seconds (integer)
- view_count (integer)
- like_count (integer)
- primary_topic

Also report the total number of videos you considered and confirm each video's published date falls in 2024–2025. Accuracy of numbers matters — copy them exactly from the API responses. This data will be used to build an Excel report, so do not approximate.
Research Fireship top 10 videos

You are building an Excel artifact for a tech trend report. Work ONLY inside the workspace directory: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-tech-report-excel-notion/workspace

A staged JSON with all the data you need already exists at: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-tech-report-excel-notion/workspace/video_data.json
Read it first (use python or file read). It contains:
- "videos": list of 10 dicts, each with keys: video_id, title, published_date, duration_seconds, view_count, like_count, primary_topic
- "topic_summary": list of 5 dicts, each with keys: topic, video_count, total_views, avg_duration (already computed, sorted by total_views descending)
- "total_views", "report_title"

TASK: Create the file Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx in the workspace directory (exact filename). Use the mcp__excel__* tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, rename_worksheet, format_range as needed) or python with openpyxl if available. The final workbook must contain exactly two sheets:

1) Sheet named "Videos" — one header row + one row per video (10 data rows), columns IN THIS ORDER:
   Video_ID | Title | Published_Date | Duration_Seconds | View_Count | Like_Count | Primary_Topic
   Use the values from video_data.json verbatim (no rounding/alteration).

2) Sheet named "Topic_Summary" — one header row + one row per distinct topic (5 data rows), columns IN THIS ORDER:
   Topic | Video_Count | Total_Views | Avg_Duration
   Use the values from video_data.json "topic_summary" verbatim.

VERIFY before returning: read back the workbook (mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata / read_data_from_excel) and confirm both sheet names exist, row counts are 11 (Videos) and 6 (Topic_Summary) including headers, and spot-check a few cell values (e.g., Videos row for Nl7aCUsWykg has view_count 3878491; Topic_Summary AI row has video_count 5, total_views 13202451, avg_duration 284.2).

DELIVERABLE — return: the absolute path of Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx, the exact sheet names, row counts, and confirmation that data was written and verified. Do not create any other files.
Build Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx

You are performing external writes (Notion page, Google Calendar event, email) for a tech trend report. Work ONLY inside workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-tech-report-excel-notion/workspace

CONTEXT/DATA: Read /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-tech-report-excel-notion/workspace/video_data.json and /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-tech-report-excel-notion/workspace/email_template.txt to get exact numbers and the email formatting template. Key facts:
- Report title: "Fireship Tech Trends Q1 2026"
- Top 10 most-viewed Fireship videos (2024-2025) were analyzed; 5 distinct topics.
- Topic_Summary (by total views desc): AI (5 videos, 13,202,451 views), Security (2 videos, 4,394,826 views), Linux (1 video, 2,891,861 views), Programming (1 video, 2,496,715 views), Quantum Computing (1 video, 2,329,914 views).
- Overall: AI dominates — 5 of the top 10 videos and 13.2M of 25.3M total views; Security also prominent (2 videos incl. the CrowdStrike outage and Internet Archive hacks).
- The full report file is Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx.

TASK 1 — NOTION PAGE: Create a new page titled "Fireship Tech Trends Q1 2026" in the team knowledge base.
- First call mcp__notion__API-post-search (query something like "Knowledge Base" or similar) to locate the team knowledge base page. If a suitable knowledge base page exists, create the new page as a child of it (parent page_id). If none is found, create the page at workspace level (parent with no page_id) — do not fail.
- Page content (use mcp__notion__API-post-page with "children", or create page then mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children):
  1) A heading (heading_1 or heading_2) introducing the report, e.g. "Overview" or "Fireship Tech Trends — Q1 2026".
  2) A paragraph summarizing overall findings (AI dominance: 5 of top 10 videos are AI-related with 13.2M combined views; Security is the #2 topic; full details in the Excel report).
  3) A structured block listing the TOP 5 technology topics by total view count with their video counts and total views. A Notion "table" block is preferred: create a table with header row [Topic, Video Count, Total Views] plus 5 rows (AI/5/13,202,451; Security/2/4,394,826; Linux/1/2,891,861; Programming/1/2,496,715; Quantum Computing/1/2,329,914). If tables are problematic, use a bulleted list instead — but a table is strongly preferred. Ensure all 5 topics are present.

TASK 2 — GOOGLE CALENDAR: 
- First call mcp__google_calendar__list_events with timeMin 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z and timeMax 2026-03-31T23:59:59Z and check whether any event titled "Tech Review" already exists in March 2026. (Note: the main agent already checked and found none, but re-verify.)
- Then create a NEW weekly recurring event: summary "Tech Review Meeting", start 2026-03-09T14:00:00 (timeZone UTC), end 2026-03-09T15:00:00 (timeZone UTC), recurrence ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY"]. 

TASK 3 — EMAIL: Send an email to techteam@company.com using mcp__emails__send_email. Use the subject from the template: "[Tech Trends] Fireship Q1 2026 Report Available" (it references the tech trend report). Body must:
- summarize which technology topics appeared most in the top videos (AI appeared most — 5 of 10 videos; followed by Security, Linux, Programming, Quantum Computing),
- state the most viewed topic (AI) with its total views (13,202,451),
- mention that the new weekly Tech Review Meeting is scheduled for Mondays 14:00-15:00 UTC starting March 9, 2026,
- inform the team the full report is available in Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx.
Follow the structure/tone of email_template.txt and fill in its placeholders.

DELIVERABLE — return: the Notion page URL/id, the calendar event id (and confirmation of recurrence + no duplicate pre-existing Tech Review event), and the email send status. Do not create other artifacts.
